title: Best Hangover Pills of 2026: Our Picks and What Actually Works

author: DHM Guide Team
content:
No pill reliably stops a hangover. Aspirin tablets like Blowfish ease the morning-after headache, at some cost to your stomach. DHM supplements, taken while you drink, have the most interesting research, though most of it was done in rats and mice. Probiotic pills like Myrkl lowered blood alcohol in one small company-funded study that never asked how people felt the next day. Expect any of them to help at the margins, not to replace water, food and a slower pace.

Our picks, if you want a DHM supplement: [No Days Wasted DHM Detox](https://www.amazon.com/dp/B0D4BWK6PH?tag=dhmguide-20) if you want 1,000 mg of DHM plus L-cysteine and milk thistle in one capsule ($1.93 a serving). [Double Wood DHM](https://www.amazon.com/dp/B074N712FM?tag=dhmguide-20) for plain DHM at $0.80 a serving. [NusaPure DHM](https://www.amazon.com/dp/B08B32XBRB?tag=dhmguide-20) if you only care about price: $0.48 for a 1,000 mg serving, the lowest we track. For the morning-after headache, Blowfish works if aspirin is safe for you, and plain aspirin with a cup of coffee does nearly the same thing for less.

> **This is not medical advice.** This guide compares products based on their labels and published research. It is not a substitute for a doctor or pharmacist who knows your health history. Most hangover pills are sold as dietary supplements, which the FDA does not review for safety or effectiveness before they go on sale. **Talk to your doctor or pharmacist before trying any hangover product if** you are pregnant or breastfeeding, have liver, kidney, stomach, or bleeding problems, or take any regular medicine, especially blood thinners, antidepressants, sedatives, seizure medicines, or diabetes medicine. **Get emergency help right away (call 911 in the US)** if someone who has been drinking is confused, can't stay awake, is vomiting while drowsy, has slow or irregular breathing, or has pale or bluish skin. Those are signs of alcohol poisoning, and no pill helps with that.

## What "Hangover Pills" Actually Are

The label covers products that work in unrelated ways, and buying one while expecting another is the usual route to disappointment.

1. Painkiller pills are taken the morning after. They contain a real over-the-counter drug, usually aspirin and often caffeine. Blowfish and Alka-Seltzer are the best-known. They treat the headache and the grogginess and nothing else.
2. DHM supplements are taken while drinking or before bed. DHM (dihydromyricetin) is a plant compound. Most commercial DHM is extracted from vine tea (Ampelopsis grossedentata), and it is also found in the Japanese raisin tree, Hovenia dulcis. Brands include No Days Wasted, Double Wood, Cheers, Flyby, Toniiq and NusaPure.
3. Probiotic pills are taken before the first drink. Myrkl is the main one. Its bacteria can break down alcohol in the gut, and the aim is that less of it reaches your blood.
4. Vitamin, electrolyte and herbal blends: B vitamins, milk thistle, prickly pear, ginger, L-cysteine. These are sold alone or mixed into the products above.
5. Activated charcoal is sold to "absorb" alcohol. It binds alcohol poorly, and we don't recommend it.

The research behind each type is covered in our article on [whether hangover pills actually work](/never-hungover/do-hangover-pills-actually-work). This page is about what to buy and what to skip.

## Do Hangover Pills Work? What the Research Says

A hangover isn't one problem. It's several at once: poor sleep, inflammation, stomach irritation, mild dehydration, the toxic by-product acetaldehyde that your liver makes while breaking down alcohol, and a rebound in brain chemistry as alcohol wears off. A pill that targets one of these can only ever help with part of the picture.

Two systematic reviews have looked at the research as a whole. In 2005, Pittler, Verster and Ernst reviewed the trials in the *BMJ* and found no compelling evidence that any conventional or complementary remedy prevented or treated hangovers.

A 2022 review in *Addiction*, from researchers at King's College London, found a handful of ingredients with a positive result in a single small study each: Hovenia dulcis fruit extract, L-cysteine, clove extract, red ginseng and Korean pear juice among them. The authors rated all of that evidence as very low quality and said no remedy could be recommended with confidence.

The best of these products can take the edge off for some people. None reliably prevents a hangover, and none undoes a heavy night. Drinking less is the only method that works every time, and our guide on [how to prevent a hangover](/never-hungover/how-to-prevent-a-hangover) covers the habits with the best evidence.

## How We Chose the Best Hangover Pills

We didn't run lab tests or a clinical trial. We read labels and listings and checked five things, and you can use the same checklist on any product you find.

- The active ingredient and its amount. DHM products run from 300 mg to 1,000 mg per serving, and no human dose has been established, so we state the dose for each one.
- Cost per serving rather than per bottle. Flyby's four-serving pack costs $14.49, which is $3.62 a night. NusaPure's 60-serving bottle works out to $0.48.
- Whether the label lists every ingredient with its amount. "Proprietary blends" hide the doses.
- Whether the add-ins have any research behind them. L-cysteine and prickly pear each have one small human trial. Most of the rest pad the ingredient list.
- Who should avoid the product, and which common medicines it interacts with.

Prices are from our last check of the Amazon listings. They change often, so confirm on the product page before you buy.

## How DHM Is Supposed to Work, and Where the Evidence Stands

DHM became popular after a 2012 study in the *Journal of Neuroscience* by Shen and colleagues at UCLA. In rats, DHM reduced signs of intoxication and withdrawal, apparently by acting on the brain's GABA receptors, the same system alcohol affects. Later lab and animal studies suggest it may speed the clearance of alcohol and acetaldehyde and protect liver cells from alcohol-related stress.

Almost all of that work was done in animals or cells. The human studies that exist tested Hovenia dulcis extracts, which contain DHM among many other compounds, and they are small. No large, independent human trial has shown that a DHM supplement prevents hangovers. Some people report a clear difference and others notice nothing, which is what you'd expect from an ingredient with a weak, variable effect.

There is also no established human dose. Products run from 300 mg to 1,000 mg a serving, so follow the label. There's no strong human evidence favoring one timing either; most labels say to take it while drinking or before bed, with water. Our [DHM dosage guide](/never-hungover/dhm-dosage-guide-2025) covers amounts in more detail, and our [supplement reviews](/reviews) rank every brand we track.

**Safety notes on DHM:** it's generally well tolerated in the studies done so far, but long-term human safety data are limited. Because it acts on GABA receptors, be cautious combining it with sedatives, sleep aids, or anti-anxiety medicines, and ask a pharmacist if you take any regular medicine. Our [DHM medication interactions guide](/never-hungover/dhm-medication-interactions-safety-guide-2025) explains which combinations deserve a second look.

## Blowfish for Hangovers: Best for a Morning-After Headache

Blowfish is an effervescent tablet you dissolve in water. A dose of two tablets contains 1,000 mg of aspirin and caffeine. Unlike DHM supplements, it's an FDA-regulated over-the-counter drug, sold under the same rules as other aspirin-and-caffeine pain relievers.

Aspirin eases a pounding head and caffeine blunts the grogginess, so for a hangover that is mostly headache, it works. It does little for nausea, rehydrates you only by the glass of water you dissolve it in, and does nothing about the causes.

The cost is to your stomach. Aspirin irritates the stomach lining and thins the blood, and alcohol irritates the stomach too; the US aspirin label warns about stomach bleeding for anyone who has three or more drinks a day. Generic aspirin and a cup of coffee give you similar ingredients for less.

Take it the morning after, with food and water, not before bed while alcohol is still in your system. Skip it if you have ulcers, reflux, or bleeding problems, take blood thinners, are allergic to aspirin, are pregnant, or are under 18. Our full [Blowfish review](/never-hungover/blowfish-hangover-review) and our guide to [aspirin and alcohol](/never-hungover/aspirin-and-alcohol) explain the risks in more detail.

## Alka-Seltzer for Hangovers: An Old Standby With a Salt Catch

Alka-Seltzer Original is another fizzy aspirin tablet. Each tablet contains 325 mg of aspirin with sodium bicarbonate (baking soda) and citric acid, which together act as an antacid. That makes it a reasonable fit for a morning with a headache and a sour stomach at once.

- **Pros:** cheap and stocked everywhere; the antacid can settle an upset stomach; the drink gets some water into you.
- **Cons:** it's still aspirin, with the same stomach-bleeding and blood-thinning concerns as Blowfish. It's also high in sodium, which matters if you have high blood pressure, heart or kidney problems, or have been told to limit salt.

Read the box. The Alka-Seltzer name covers many products, and some "Plus" cold and flu versions contain other drugs, including acetaminophen (Tylenol). Check the Drug Facts label so you don't double up on painkillers.

If acid and burning are your main symptoms rather than headache, our guide to [heartburn after drinking](/never-hungover/heartburn-after-drinking) covers gentler options. And if you're wondering whether a different painkiller would be better, our articles on [ibuprofen and alcohol](/never-hungover/ibuprofen-and-alcohol) and [Tylenol and alcohol](/never-hungover/tylenol-and-alcohol) compare the stomach and liver risks of each. In short: never take acetaminophen to "head off" a hangover, because alcohol and acetaminophen together can stress the liver.

## Myrkl: The Probiotic "Pre-Drink" Pill

Myrkl, from the Swedish company De Faire Medical, takes a different approach. You take it before drinking, and its probiotic bacteria are meant to start breaking down alcohol in your gut so less of it reaches your bloodstream.

- **Pros:** more published human research than most hangover products; looks low risk for healthy adults.
- **Cons:** the main human study was small, company-funded, and measured blood alcohol rather than how people felt the next morning. The idea also has a built-in limit: alcohol is absorbed quickly and mostly broken down in the liver, where gut bacteria can't reach.

Myrkl does not make you sober, and it must never be used to decide whether you're fine to drive. There is no good evidence that it makes hangovers better for most people, and online reviews split between people who swear by it and people who noticed nothing. Our full [Myrkl review](/never-hungover/myrkl-review) has the details. If you're interested in the probiotic idea, [ZBiotics](/never-hungover/zbiotics-review) is a related product, though it's a drink rather than a pill and targets acetaldehyde instead of alcohol itself.

## Other Ingredients You'll See in Hangover Pills

Most hangover supplements mix several of these. Only the first two have a human hangover trial behind them, and each has just one small one.

- Prickly pear (Opuntia): a 2004 randomized trial in *Archives of Internal Medicine* found the extract reduced nausea, dry mouth and loss of appetite, but not headache. Our [DHM vs prickly pear comparison](/never-hungover/dhm-vs-prickly-pear-hangovers) looks at both.
- L-cysteine, an amino acid the body uses to make glutathione, which helps clear acetaldehyde. A small Finnish study suggested some benefit; our [L-cysteine guide](/never-hungover/l-cysteine-for-hangover) has the details.
- Milk thistle is the best-known liver herb. Its human results for liver health are mixed, and almost nobody has tested it on hangovers.
- B vitamins and electrolytes are low risk and cheap to add, which is most of why they appear on so many labels. There's little evidence they prevent hangovers.
- Hovenia and turmeric drinks and pills are big sellers in Korea and Japan. Our guide to [Korean and Japanese hangover pills](/never-hungover/korean-japanese-hangover-pills) covers what's in them.
- Activated charcoal is the one we'd skip. It binds alcohol poorly and can stop medicines taken around the same time from being absorbed. Our [activated charcoal article](/never-hungover/activated-charcoal-hangover) explains why.

## Hangover Pills to Be Careful With

- "Night-time" or "PM" products contain a sedating antihistamine such as diphenhydramine or doxylamine, which stacks drowsiness on top of alcohol. Don't take them on a night you drink.
- Check multi-symptom "morning after" products for acetaminophen, APAP or paracetamol, and never take any of them before bed after drinking.
- "Proprietary blends" list ingredients without amounts, so you can't tell whether you're getting a meaningful dose of anything.
- Be wary of any label that promises to stop a hangover completely or let you drink more without consequences. No product has evidence for that.
- Taking a DHM supplement, a painkiller and a sleep aid on the same night multiplies the chance of side effects and interactions.

## How to Use Hangover Pills Sensibly

These habits matter more than the brand you pick.

1. Match the pill to the job. DHM and probiotic products go before or during drinking. Painkillers are for the morning after, never before bed.
2. Eat before and while you drink, since food slows alcohol absorption.
3. Have a glass of water between drinks. Our [Pedialyte vs Gatorade comparison](/never-hungover/pedialyte-vs-gatorade-hangover) covers rehydration drinks if you want more than water.
4. Pace yourself. The body clears roughly one standard drink an hour, and no pill speeds that up enough to matter for driving.
5. Protect your sleep. Much of next-day fog is simply a short, broken night.
6. Try one product at a time. If you change three things at once, you won't know what helped.

For a full checklist of what to do before a night out, our guide on [what to take before drinking](/never-hungover/what-to-take-before-drinking) pulls it together, and our [hangover kit ideas](/never-hungover/hangover-kit-ideas) cover what to keep on hand.

## When a Hangover Means You Should See a Doctor

Most hangovers are miserable but harmless and pass within a day. Some symptoms are a sign of something more serious. **Get medical help right away (call 911 in the US)** if someone who has been drinking:

- is confused, can't stay awake, or can't be woken
- is vomiting while drowsy or vomiting repeatedly
- has slow, shallow, or irregular breathing
- has pale or bluish skin or feels very cold
- has a seizure

Also see a doctor if you notice black or tarry stools or vomit that looks like coffee grounds after taking aspirin, if you have severe stomach pain, or if you might have taken more acetaminophen than the label allows (call Poison Control at **1-800-222-1222** in the US, even if you feel fine).

If you get shaky, sweaty, anxious, or have a racing heart when you go a day or two without drinking, that's different from a hangover. It can be a sign of alcohol withdrawal, which can be dangerous, so talk to a doctor rather than trying to manage it with supplements.

## The Bottom Line

If you want to try DHM, buy [Double Wood](https://www.amazon.com/dp/B074N712FM?tag=dhmguide-20) for a cheap first bottle, [NusaPure](https://www.amazon.com/dp/B08B32XBRB?tag=dhmguide-20) once you know it suits you, or [No Days Wasted](https://www.amazon.com/dp/B0D4BWK6PH?tag=dhmguide-20) if you want L-cysteine and milk thistle in the same capsule. Expect a modest effect at best.

For a morning-after headache, an aspirin product like Blowfish works, and Alka-Seltzer adds an antacid if your stomach is sour too. Take either with food, never before bed, and only if aspirin is safe for you.

Skip Myrkl unless you're curious and the price doesn't bother you; there's no evidence it changes how you feel the next day. Skip activated charcoal entirely. You can see every DHM brand we track side by side in our [supplement reviews](/reviews) or [compare any two](/compare).

## Frequently Asked Questions

**What is the best hangover pill?**

It depends on what you want it to do. For a supplement taken while drinking, a DHM product is the most popular choice, with No Days Wasted offering the most complete formula and Double Wood the best value. For a morning-after headache, an aspirin-and-caffeine product like Blowfish works for many people. No pill reliably prevents a hangover, so treat any of them as an add-on to water, food, and pacing.

**Do hangover pills actually work?**

Some can help a little, but none are reliable. Large research reviews have found no strong evidence that any pill prevents or cures a hangover. Painkiller pills can ease a headache. DHM has promising animal research and limited human data. A few ingredients, such as prickly pear and L-cysteine, have small studies suggesting modest benefits for some symptoms.

**When should I take a hangover pill?**

It depends on the type. DHM supplements and probiotic products like Myrkl are taken before or while drinking, or before bed. Painkiller pills like Blowfish and Alka-Seltzer are for the morning after, taken with food and water. Never take aspirin, ibuprofen, or acetaminophen before bed while alcohol is still in your system.

**Is Alka-Seltzer good for a hangover?**

Alka-Seltzer Original combines aspirin with an antacid, so it can help with a headache and an upset stomach at the same time. But it's still aspirin, which can irritate a stomach already irritated by alcohol, and it's high in sodium. Check the label, since some Alka-Seltzer Plus cold products contain other drugs, including acetaminophen in some formulas.

**Is Blowfish better than DHM?**

They do different jobs. Blowfish is an aspirin-and-caffeine pain reliever for the morning after, and it eases headaches for many people, but it doesn't address anything beyond symptoms and carries stomach risks with alcohol. DHM is taken while drinking and aims to support how your body handles alcohol, but the human evidence is still limited. Some people use DHM while drinking and save a painkiller for the morning only if they need it.

**Does Myrkl work?**

There is no good evidence yet that Myrkl makes hangovers noticeably better for most people. Its main human study was small, company-funded, and measured blood alcohol rather than how people felt the next day. It looks low risk for healthy adults, but it does not make you sober and should never be used to judge whether you're fine to drive.

**Are hangover pills safe?**

Most are low risk for healthy adults when used as directed, but "supplement" doesn't mean risk-free. Aspirin-based pills can cause stomach bleeding when combined with alcohol. DHM may interact with sedatives and some other medicines. Products sold as supplements aren't reviewed by the FDA before sale. Talk to a doctor or pharmacist first if you take regular medicine, are pregnant, or have liver, kidney, stomach, or bleeding problems.

**Can I take a hangover pill and still drive?**

No. No hangover pill lowers your blood alcohol fast enough to make driving safe, and none of them make you sober. Your body clears alcohol at roughly one standard drink per hour, and that varies a lot between people. If you've been drinking, don't drive.
